Verdicts: quality: no criterion stated by the authors (all configurations); cost: not measured

Tasks: 73 FeatureArc tasks (stratified by language and chain length, defect-screened, manually checked). Configurations: 10 agents. Baseline: none (within-agent comparison of first stage vs whole feature; after-pass vs after-fail stages within task-stage groups). Held constant: initial code, stage specifications, hidden checks, four-hour stage budget, no failure feedback, no rollback, offline containers. Not held constant: harness for GPT-6 Astra (Codex CLI), provider-specific context and reasoning controls; cross-agent scores conflate model and harness. Acceptance tests: hidden F2P and P2P suites validated on reference states, plus chain-level suites. Repetitions: Not stated. Human intervention: none

Pooled success falls from 62.7% (first stage) to 28.5% (chain gate); every agent loses 26.0-38.4 points; Claude Opus 5.5 best (83.6% -> 49.3%), DeepSeek V4 Pro lowest gate (17.8%); Spearman rho 0.87 between m0 and gate. 25.3% of runs passing the last-stage gate fail the chain gate; 2.7% of runs with a failed stage recover. Chain gate 44.4% on two-stage tasks vs 1.5% with five or more stages. Next-stage F2P 70.2% after a passed stage vs 22.6% after a failed one; inherited defects in 72.9% of failed later stages; earlier failures unnoticed in 94.9%; green self-tests pass F2P in 52.7% (24.5% after a failed stage); 87.5% of red results dismissed. No significance tests between agents (bootstrap intervals, e.g. Hunyuan gate 23.3-45.2%)

Distinguished first-stage from whole-feature success and located failures (inheritance, missed detection); agent rankings broadly stable across metrics. Trajectory labels validated against blind human annotation. Repeatability: not assessed. Limitations of the comparison stated: cross-agent scores reflect joint model-harness performance; threat that tasks may not cover all real-world workflows

Threat stated: FeatureArc may not cover the full range of real-world feature-development workflows (mitigated by four languages, seven domains, stratified tasks). Gaps: evolving a feature autonomously without human checks between stages remains hard; agents need to check earlier requirements and verify their failure explanations

Authors (Tencent Hunyuan) evaluate their own pre-release Hunyuan 4 Preview and use it as one of three LLM judges; construction used GPT-5.5 (steps 1-3), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (step 4), Claude Sonnet 5 (step 5). Reporting inconsistencies: text says Claude Opus 5.5 'leads every metric', but Gemini 3.8 Flash ties its chain-level P2P failure (5.5%, Table III); 100 candidate tasks were sampled and 7 excluded for defects (p 4), which leaves 93, yet the final set has 73 tasks and the 20 further removals are not explained. 'Published task manifests' mentioned but no link to benchmark, code or data. No pre-registration. Languages: Python 21, Go 20, TypeScript 18, Rust 14 tasks. Claude Code and Codex CLI versions not stated. Same group as FeatureLoop (rayyan-800486546)
